title: Specialization lifting and noncollapse in etale charts of a quasi-separated space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume its diagonal $X\to X\times_S X$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests, meaning that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $a:U\to X$ be any representable etale morphism from a scheme, in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $p\leadsto q$ when $q$ lies in the closure of $\{p\}$. Then $|a|$ is continuous. If $x\leadsto a(u)$ for $x\in|X|$ and $u\in U$, there is $u'\in U$ with $u'\leadsto u$ and $a(u')=x$. Moreover, if $u'\leadsto u$ and $a(u')=a(u)$, then $u'=u$. No surjectivity, finite-type, or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tags 03IL, lemma-decent-specialization, and 03K5, lemma-decent-no-specializations-map-to-same-point; quasi-separated implies decent by Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres. Continuity is immediate from the cited final-topology definition.

proof.text: Continuity follows directly from [def-a1-space-point-topology]: inverse images of opens are open under every etale scheme chart, including $a$. For either specialization assertion fix $u\in U$. Choose an affine open of $S$ containing its image and then an affine open neighbourhood $W\subset U$ of $u$ mapping into it, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Every generalization of $u$ in $U$ lies in $W$, since opens are stable under generalization. The restricted $p:W\to X$ remains representable etale: on each scheme test its map is an open immersion followed by the base change of $a$, so use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Put $R=W\times_XW$ with projections $s,t$. It is a scheme and $s,t$ are etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tags 03K2 and 03IM, beginning of each proof: replace the chart by an affine neighbourhood; the affine-base refinement retains the stated relative hypothesis.

proof.text: The scheme projections $s,t$ are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence generalizations lift along them by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift]. Their fibres are discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], together with the subspace homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Thus comparable points of $R$ having the same $s$-image, or the same $t$-image, coincide: a specialization inside a discrete subspace is equality. Also $W$ has antisymmetric specialization, since two mutually specializing points are generic points of the same irreducible singleton closure and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] makes that generic point unique.

source.place: Remark recall, points (1) and (2), used in Tags 03K2 and 03IM; scheme sobriety supplies antisymmetry.

proof.text: For the lifting assertion let $x\leadsto p(u)$. By [lem-sfb-relative-qs-affine-chart-point-fibres], the sets $A=p^{-1}(\{x\})$ and $B=(p s)^{-1}(\{x\})=(p t)^{-1}(\{x\})$ are finite. Set $C=\bigcup_{w\in A}\overline{\{w\}}\subset W$ and $D=\bigcup_{r\in B}\overline{\{r\}}\subset R$. These are closed, and their points are precisely the specializations of members of $A$ and $B$, respectively. This includes empty $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization, finite fibre sets and the closed sets T and T-prime.

proof.text: We have $s^{-1}(C)=D=t^{-1}(C)$. For example, continuity gives $D\subset s^{-1}(C)$. If $s(r)\in C$, choose $w\in A$ with $w\leadsto s(r)$. Flat generalization lifting [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift], using etaleness and [def-weil-etale-morphism], gives $r\prime\leadsto r$ with $s(r\prime)=w$; then $r\prime\in B$, so $r\in D$. Repeat for $t$. The continuity and point-surjectivity assertions of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] apply: any two points of $W$ with the same $p$-image are the two projections of a point of $R$. Hence the equality of the two inverse images proves that $C$ is saturated for $p$: if one such point is in $C$, the other is in $C$.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization, proof that the finite-fibre closure is invariant under the relation.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $I=p(W)$ is open in $|X|$ and $p:W\to I$ is a continuous open surjection. As $C$ is saturated, $I\setminus p(C)=p(W\setminus C)$ is open in $I$. Thus $p(C)$ is closed in $I$. The open $I$ contains $p(u)$, so it contains its generalization $x$; therefore $A$ is nonempty and $x\in p(C)$. Closedness and $x\leadsto p(u)$ give $p(u)\in p(C)$. Saturation now gives $u\in C$. By the definition of $C$ some $u\prime\in A$ specializes to $u$, which is the required lift, also as a point of the original $U$.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization, closed invariant set descends to the closure of the general point; saturation yields the chosen lift directly.

proof.text: For noncollapse take $v_0=u$, $v_1=u\prime$ with $v_1\leadsto v_0$ and common image $y$. The fibre $p^{-1}(\{y\})$ is finite by [lem-sfb-relative-qs-affine-chart-point-fibres]. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] choose $r_0\in R$ with $t(r_0)=v_0$ and $s(r_0)=v_1$. Recursively, given $r_n$ with $t(r_n)=v_n$, $s(r_n)=v_{n+1}$ and $v_{n+1}\leadsto v_n$, lift this generalization through the flat projection $t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. This gives $r_{n+1}\leadsto r_n$ with $t(r_{n+1})=v_{n+1}$. Define $v_{n+2}=s(r_{n+1})$. Continuity gives $v_{n+2}\leadsto v_{n+1}$ and $p s=p t$ gives $p(v_{n+2})=y$. This constructs all points in the same finite fibre.

source.place: Tag 03IM, lemma-no-specializations-map-to-same-point, recursive tower of lifted specializations.

proof.text: If $v_{n+2}=v_{n+1}$, then $s(r_{n+1})=s(r_n)$ and $r_{n+1}\leadsto r_n$. By the discrete-fibre consequence in step 2, $r_{n+1}=r_n$, and applying $t$ gives $v_{n+1}=v_n$. Thus any adjacent equality propagates backwards to $v_1=v_0$. If $v_1\ne v_0$, every adjacent pair in the chain is distinct. Any repeated pair $v_i=v_j$ with $i<j$ would, by transitivity and antisymmetry of specialization on $W$, force an adjacent equality. Consequently all $v_n$ would be distinct, contradicting the finite fibre in step 6. Hence $u\prime=u$. The reduction to $W$ lost no comparable point because $W$ contains every generalization of $u$.

source.place: Tag 03IM, lemma-no-specializations-map-to-same-point, propagation of equality and contradiction to finite fibres.
